seoTitle: How to Print Double Sided in Canva (Easy Setup)
metaDescription: Format multi-page Canva designs for double-sided printing by aligning front and back layouts, enabling bleed, and choosing the right export settings.
intro: Getting a brochure, business card, or flyer to line up correctly on both sides when printed requires a bit of careful setup in Canva. This guide covers structuring your front and back pages, enabling print bleed, and configuring the export and printer settings so your double-sided materials come out aligned.

steps.heading: Structure your front and back pages
steps.body: Set page one as your front layout and page two as your back layout within the same project.

steps.heading: Enable rulers and print bleed
steps.body: Turn on rulers, guides, and print bleed margins to keep design elements safe from being cut off.

steps.heading: Align elements symmetrically
steps.body: Match text blocks and graphics precisely so the front and back stay aligned when printed back-to-back.

steps.heading: Handle backgrounds and graphics carefully
steps.body: Check that background colors and graphics extend consistently across the layout borders on both pages.

steps.heading: Export as a Print PDF
steps.body: Open the Share menu and choose the Print PDF format, checking the flatten PDF option for high-quality output.

steps.heading: Configure your printer for duplex printing
steps.body: Adjust your local printer settings for short-edge or long-edge binding depending on how the design should flip.

faq.question: What's the difference between short-edge and long-edge binding?
faq.answer: Short-edge binding flips the page along its shorter side, while long-edge flips along the longer side — the correct choice depends on your specific document orientation and printer setup.

faq.question: Do I need to enable print bleed for double-sided printing?
faq.answer: Yes, enabling bleed margins helps keep your design elements safe from being cut off during trimming.

faq.question: Can I print double-sided at home?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as your printer supports duplex printing, though you may also send the exported PDF to a professional print shop.

faq.question: Why don't my front and back pages line up when printed?
faq.answer: Misalignment often comes down to inconsistent margins or bleed settings between the two pages, so double-check symmetry before exporting.
